cmspages.content: Bakra Mandi is an online bakra mandi for Eid ul Adha: qurbani bakray, dumbay, gaye, bail, oont and bhains from farms, homes and mandis across Pakistan — with teeth, live weight and price on every ad, verified sellers and direct contact. cmspages.title: How It Works
cmspages.content:
Selling

  • Tap Sell your animal and choose the animal and breed
  • Add clear photos (side, face and teeth), the teeth, live weight and gender, and your price
  • Buyers call, WhatsApp or chat with you — agree a time to see the animal

Buying

  • Browse by animal, breed, city, mandi or budget
  • Ask for a video and the teeth photo, then see the animal in person
  • Check its age and health, weigh it if you buy by weight, then pay

cmspages.title: Safety Tips
cmspages.content:
• Never send an advance, booking or token payment for an animal you haven't seen.
  • See the animal in daylight at the farm or mandi: check the teeth, eyes, horns, ears and how it walks.
  • Buying by weight? Weigh it on a scale in front of you.
  • For a qurbani share (hissa), deal with an organiser you can visit — ask for the animal, the address and a video of the qurbani.
  • Ticks can spread Congo fever: wear full sleeves at the mandi, check the animal for ticks and never crush one with bare hands.
  • Prefer verified sellers, and report anything suspicious.

faqs.question: Is posting an ad free?
faqs.answer: Yes — your first ad is free. Beoparis and farms with many animals can take a plan for more ads and featured placement.

faqs.question: How can I tell an animal's age?
faqs.answer: From its teeth. 'Kheera' means it still has only milk teeth. 'Do dant' — two permanent front teeth — usually means a goat or sheep is about a year old and a cow or buffalo about two. Ask the seller for a clear photo of the teeth, and check them yourself before paying.

faqs.question: At what age is an animal valid for qurbani?
faqs.answer: As widely followed in Pakistan: a goat or sheep should be at least one year old (many scholars also accept a healthy dumba of six months or more that looks a year old), a cow, bull or buffalo two years, and a camel five years. If you are unsure, ask your local scholar.

faqs.question: Which defects make an animal unsuitable?
faqs.answer: Commonly listed defects are: blind or blind in one eye, so lame that it can't walk to the place of slaughter, very weak or clearly sick, a large part of an ear or the tail cut off, a horn broken from the root, or most teeth missing. Check these in person — and ask a scholar about anything in between.

faqs.question: How does a qurbani share (hissa) work?
faqs.answer: A cow, bull, buffalo or camel can be shared by up to seven people, each paying for one share. Choose an organiser you can visit: ask which animal it is, the address, the qurbani day, how the meat reaches you and whether you'll get a video of the qurbani.

faqs.question: How do I buy safely?
faqs.answer: Never send an advance or 'booking' payment for an animal you haven't seen. Meet at the farm or mandi in daylight, check the animal, weigh it if you buy by weight, and pay only when it is handed over.

faqs.question: How do I protect myself from Congo virus at the mandi?
faqs.answer: Congo fever spreads through ticks on animals. Wear full sleeves and closed shoes, check the animal for ticks, don't crush ticks with bare hands, and see a doctor if you get a fever after visiting a mandi or handling animals.

faqs.question: Can the seller keep my animal until Eid?
faqs.answer: Many sellers do (rakhwali) — look for 'Kept until Eid' on the ad and agree the feeding, the fee and who is responsible if the animal falls sick, in writing.

faqs.question: How do I become a verified seller?
faqs.answer: Add your mobile number and upload your CNIC (front and back) from My account → Seller verification. Once approved, the verified badge shows on all your ads.

blogposts.title: Buying your qurbani animal: the checklist
blogposts.excerpt: Teeth, health, weight and a fair price — step by step.
blogposts.content:
1. Teeth first

Look at the front teeth: two permanent teeth (do dant) usually means the animal has reached qurbani age.

2. Health

Bright eyes, a clean nose, firm walk and a good appetite. Check for ticks and for any wound or limp.

3. Weight and price

Buying by weight? Weigh it in front of you. Compare a few animals of the same breed and size.

4. Pay safely

Only when the animal is handed over — never an advance for an animal you haven't seen.

blogposts.title: Teeth and age: is the animal qurbani-ready?
blogposts.excerpt: What kheera, do dant and chaar dant tell you.
blogposts.content:
Kheera

Only milk teeth — usually too young for qurbani.

Do dant (2 teeth)

Two permanent front teeth: a goat or sheep is usually around a year old, a cow or buffalo around two.

Chaar dant and more

Four or more permanent teeth: an older, mature animal.

When unsure, ask your local scholar.

blogposts.title: Congo virus at Eid: staying safe at the mandi
blogposts.excerpt: Ticks, gloves and what to do if you get a fever.
blogposts.content:
Why it matters

Congo fever spreads through ticks on animals, and cases rise around Eid.

At the mandi

Wear full sleeves and closed shoes, and check the animal for ticks before you bring it home.

At home

Keep the animal's place clean and never crush a tick with bare hands. See a doctor for any fever after handling animals.
